title: Block: Push, Pop and Peek a Stack
oneLiner: Check that every bracket in a string is closed in the right order, ignoring other characters.
keyTakeaway: Before every pop, ask whether the stack is empty. That one check is the difference between a stack block that works and one that throws on ")".
explanation:
Return true if the brackets (), [] and {} in s are balanced: every opener is closed by the matching closer, in the right order. Other characters are ignored, so "f(a[0]) + {b}" is balanced and "([)]" isn't.

Push openers. On a closer, the stack must be non-empty and its top must be the matching opener; then pop. A small map from closer to opener saves three if statements. The string is balanced only if the stack is empty at the end.

starterCode.python:
def is_balanced(s):
    # 1. Make an empty stack and a map from each closing bracket to its opener.
    # 2. For each character, push it if it is an opening bracket.
    # 3. If it is a closing bracket, fail when the stack is empty or its top is not the matching opener; otherwise pop.
    # 4. Ignore every other character.
    # 5. Return true only if the stack is empty at the end.
    return False

gotchas: Popping or peeking an empty stack on a closer with no opener.
Returning true at the end without checking the stack is empty, so "((" passes.

complexity.note: Each character is pushed and popped at most once; all openers can be on the stack at once.
